answer: Each identity is verified by a chain of modular squarings, with each result depending on the previous one; GPUs can speed individual operations but cannot parallelize a single chain’s sequential dependency. A Wesolowski proof lets others verify the completed work efficiently. Cloned identities do not make any chain faster: each requires its own sustained computation and elapsed time. Challenge labels such as ember, pigment, and onyx do not alter this physical bottleneck.
